(4)–(8), absorbed fractions by a direct flux linear solve checked against the EN 410 double-glazing closed form) and EN 16612:2019 edge strength; 42 cases: 7 page presets, 30 grid cases (6 glazings × 5 situations, irradiance 500–950 W/m², annealed cut / polished / heat-strengthened), 4 parameter sweeps (k, duration, γM, extra ΔT) and a hand case built from the same model, not an external published value (1/1)

Learning assumptions of both engine and reference (labelled on the page; FIV 01 of NBN S 23-002:2007 §4.4.1.3 not available): generic optical data, frame share r / cold-mass lag / rebate lag, shadow factors 1,0 / 1,25 and diffuse share 0,15, blind optics and gap coupling, restraint k = 1, 5 h peak
tolerance: temperatures and ΔT ≤ 0,02 K, αe and fg;d ≤ 10⁻⁶, utilisation ≤ 0,5 % (relative, floor 0,2), risk level exact away from the 0,5 / 1,0 borders, governing pane exact; the utilisation tile must show the reference value to 2 decimals; max utilisation deviation 0.0000 %

provenance_note: Glass centre, edge and shadow temperatures, ΔT, edge design strength, utilisation and risk level were computed by bench-src/ref/gen_glassthermalbreak.py, written from NBN S 23-002-2:2020 Annex A (closed forms A.3 / A.4 with the A.2 iteration), the NBN EN 673 gap-conductance equations and EN 16612:2019 §8 / Table A.5, not from the page code (the page solves a nodal network and iterates the optical fluxes; the reference uses the closed forms and a direct linear solve). The closed forms are independent of the page only in the cases without a blind; in the cases with a blind (22 of 42) the reference solves the blind with the same learning-assumption network as the page (hrb with blind ε 0,9, ventilation table, 8 W/m²K to the room) — a shared assumption, not an independent check. The edge / shadow / blind factors and generic optical data are learning assumptions shared by both (FIV 01 not available) — re-typed, not imported. The hand case (single clear 6 mm) is built from the same model, not an external published value.
